book_title: Mukhtasar al-Athar: The Summary of Transmitted Reports (Volume Two)

chapters.title: The Marketplace: Honest Earning, Trade, and Property
chapters.rationale: All economic dealing belongs in one sustained read — from the command to seek a livelihood through forbidden sales, usury, contracts, debt, partnership, and pre-emption — because every section answers the single question of how wealth may rightly change hands.

chapters.title: Binding Words: Oaths, Vows, and Their Atonement
chapters.rationale: Oaths, vows, and expiations form one coherent domain — the weight a person places on his own word before God — and the rules for breaking that word naturally close the thread that the rules for making it open.

chapters.title: The Body's Portion: Food, Drink, and Healing
chapters.rationale: Eating, drinking, and the treatment of illness all concern what enters and restores the body, so the lawful table and the lawful remedy — including supplication, ruqyah, and medicine — read as a single account of bodily life.

chapters.title: What We Wear: Dress, Adornment, and Fragrance
chapters.rationale: Clothing, jewelry, rings, and scent share the theme of how a believer presents himself outwardly — beauty permitted, vanity restrained — making them one chapter on the adorned self.

chapters.title: The Hunt and the Knife: Game, Slaughter, and Sacrifice
chapters.rationale: Hunting, ritual slaughter, the festival sacrifice, and the newborn's aqiqah all turn on the same act — lawfully taking an animal's life — so they belong together as the law of the blade.

chapters.title: Marriage and the Household
chapters.rationale: Everything from the call to marry through proposal, dowry, conditions, forbidden unions, conjugal life, and maintenance describes the building and ordering of a single household, the longest unbroken arc in the book.

chapters.title: When a Marriage Ends: Divorce and Separation
chapters.rationale: The many forms of ending a marriage — divorce, khul', ila, zihar, li'an, the waiting period, and what is owed afterward — are one continuous subject: the careful unwinding of the bond the previous chapter formed.

chapters.title: Freedom, Generosity, and the Division of Estates
chapters.rationale: Manumission, gifts and endowments, wills, and inheritance all govern how persons and possessions pass from one hand to another — by liberation, by bestowal, or by death — making them a single chapter on what one leaves behind.

chapters.title: Wrong and Redress: Crime, Property Disputes, and the Judge
chapters.rationale: Retaliation, blood-money, the hudud, then usurpation, trusts, lost property, testimony, evidence, and the conduct of judges all converge on one theme — how wrongs are punished and rights are vindicated before the law — closing the volume with the machinery of justice.
